## Natural history notes

A small damselfly characterized by its slender body, narrow wings held together over the back, and contrasting blue, green, orange, or black markings that vary by sex and age. In Florida, it is common around ponds, marshes, canals, ditches, lakes, wet prairies, and other sunny freshwater or brackish wetlands with emergent vegetation. Adults perch low on grasses and stems and hunt tiny flying insects, while the aquatic nymphs live among submerged vegetation and feed on small aquatic invertebrates.
